meta.description: Not a Fleetwood Mac original. Little Willie John recorded it first, released on King Records on 20 October 1955, and took it to No. 5 on the Billboard R&B chart.
meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'Need Your Love So Bad'?
meta.ogDescription: Fleetwood Mac's 1968 single is a cover. Little Willie John recorded it first, on King Records, 20 October 1955 - and it was already an R&B hit.

answer.label: Not a Fleetwood Mac original — a 1955 Little Willie John single on King
answer.originalArtistDates: 1937-1968 · American R&B and soul singer, born William Edward John
answer.sourceLine: Peter Green’s aching, string-draped 1968 single is so completely his that listeners routinely file it as a Fleetwood Mac original. It is a cover. “Need Your Love So Bad” was first recorded by Little Willie John and issued as a King Records single on 20 October 1955, written by John with his elder brother Mertis John Jr. Far from being an obscurity that Fleetwood Mac rescued, the original was a hit in its own right, reaching No. 5 on the Billboard R&B chart in 1956.

original.released: Issued as a 7-inch and 78 rpm single on King Records on 20 October 1955, backed with “Home at Last”. It was one of Little Willie John’s earliest sides for the label.
original.charted: Yes — it reached No. 5 on the Billboard R&B chart in 1956, and the B-side “Home at Last” reached No. 6.
original.writer: Mertis John Jr. and William Edward John
original.cover: Fleetwood Mac recorded it in April 1968 for Mike Vernon’s Blue Horizon label; the single was released on 5 July 1968 and reached No. 31 on the UK Singles Chart and No. 7 in the Netherlands.

trail: Wikipedia’s article on the song ↗ dates the Little Willie John single to 20 October 1955 on King Records and records its No. 5 R&B chart placing in 1956.
The MusicBrainz work entry ↗ credits both Little Willie John and Mertis John Jr. as composer and lyricist, noting Mertis as the elder brother.
Wikidata ↗ names Little Willie John as the first performer of the composition and gives October 1955 as the initial release.
The same Wikipedia article dates the Fleetwood Mac recording to April 1968 for Blue Horizon, released 5 July 1968, with strings arranged by Mickey Baker — the guitarist on John’s original session.

authors.name: Little Willie John
authors.heading: Little Willie John
authors.bio: Born William Edward John in Cullendale, Arkansas in 1937 and raised in Detroit, he signed to King Records in 1955 while still a teenager and became one of the most affecting ballad singers of the decade. “Need Your Love So Bad” was among his earliest sides for the label, cut with a New York band that included guitarist Mickey Baker. His life ended in prison in Walla Walla, Washington in 1968, the same year Fleetwood Mac’s version of his song reached the British charts. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame ↗ in 1996.

authors.name: Fleetwood Mac
authors.heading: Fleetwood Mac
authors.metaLine: British blues band · Blue Horizon single, 1968
authors.bio: The Peter Green-led Fleetwood Mac recorded the song in April 1968 for producer Mike Vernon’s Blue Horizon label, and the single appeared on 5 July 1968. It reached No. 31 on the UK Singles Chart and No. 7 in the Netherlands, and Green’s guitar tone on it became one of the most imitated sounds in British blues. The strings were arranged by Mickey Baker — the same guitarist who had played on Little Willie John’s 1955 session — though Green later said he regretted the overdubs. Nothing about the record is dishonest; the band never claimed the song, listeners simply assumed it.

authors.name: Mertis John Jr.
authors.heading: Mertis John Jr.
authors.metaLine: Elder brother of Little Willie John · co-writer
authors.bio: Mertis John Jr. was Little Willie John’s older brother and is credited as co-writer of the song alongside him. MusicBrainz lists both men as composer and lyricist of the work, and Wikidata carries the same pair of writing credits. Credits on individual pressings and compilations have not always been consistent, with some issues naming only one of the brothers. Accounts differ over how the writing split — the original King label credited only Willie John, while a 2001 biography of his brother says Mertis wrote much of it in Korea and brought it to Willie to finish, with Willie’s name restored as co-writer in 2008; BMI now credits both men.

misattribution.heading: What people get wrong
misattribution.intro: Peter Green’s 1968 recording is so identified with Fleetwood Mac that the song is regularly listed among the band’s own compositions. It is a cover of a record that was already more than a decade old and already a chart hit.

items.why: Their Blue Horizon single, recorded April 1968 and released 5 July 1968, reached No. 31 in the UK and became the definitive version for British and European listeners.
Issued as a King Records single on 20 October 1955, backed with “Home at Last”; it reached No. 5 on the Billboard R&B chart in 1956.

context.heading: Why the cover eclipsed the original
lead: The interesting question is not whether Fleetwood Mac wrote it — they plainly did not — but why the 1968 record swallowed the 1955 one so completely. Part of the answer is geography. Little Willie John’s single was an American R&B hit, No. 5 on the Billboard R&B chart in 1956, in a market British record buyers of the day largely never saw. Peter Green’s version arrived on Blue Horizon in July 1968 and charted in Britain and the Netherlands, so for a generation of European listeners it was simply where the song began.

The other part is the arrangement. Green’s reading is slower, longer and drenched in strings arranged by Mickey Baker — the very guitarist who had played on John’s King session — which gives the cover a lush, late-sixties signature that sounds nothing like a 1955 R&B ballad. Green himself came to dislike the string overdubs. The irony is that the man who connected the two records is the one detail almost nobody notices.
detailsBody: 1955 — Little Willie John records the song, written with his brother Mertis John Jr., for King Records in New York, with Mickey Baker on guitar.
20 October 1955 — King issues the single, backed with “Home at Last”.
1956 — The record reaches No. 5 on the Billboard R&B chart; the B-side reaches No. 6.
April 1968 — Fleetwood Mac record the song for Mike Vernon’s Blue Horizon label, with strings arranged by Mickey Baker.
5 July 1968 — The Fleetwood Mac single is released; it reaches No. 31 in the UK and No. 7 in the Netherlands.
Later covers include Whitesnake in 1984 and Gary Moore in 1995.
context.pull: The original was a hit. It just wasn’t a hit anywhere Britain was listening.

listen.what: Little Willie John’s original 1955 King recording
listen.source: An auto-generated upload on the “Little Willie John - Topic” channel, whose description reads “Provided to YouTube by King Records” with a ℗ 2005 Gusto Records line — Gusto holds the King catalogue. The track runs 2:16 against the 2:14 listed by MusicBrainz for the recording on the October 1955 release, confirming it is the original master rather than a later re-cut.
